pillar_reactions.evidence: Presented against his own numbers — the 5-out-of-10 shape rating and the 7-rising-to-10 mobility pain — covering strength, mobility and endurance together, three to four sessions of 30-45 minutes plus a daily 5-10 minute mobility routine, with the joints-in-alignment and 'if you don't use it, you lose it' framing. Asked the check he answered with a single 'Yep.' No questions, no elaboration, and no engagement with the compensation chain he had just described so vividly. For the pillar aimed squarely at his worst problem, that is a flat reaction.

Aimed correctly at his stated worst area — he had already rated his nutrition 'Terrible' — using the when/what/how-much frame, whole foods, no calorie counting, no chicken and rice, and specifically addressing the client-dinner problem: 'a lot of the people that Trevor works with travel a lot for work... if they're able to figure out how to do the workouts even when they're traveling, why wouldn't you be able to?' He answered with a commitment rather than a question: 'I also want to commit to that. Absolutely.' Understood and agreed, no probing.

Delivered as the answer to the thing he had named three separate times before it was presented — the push, direction, structure. Teach-a-man-to-fish, six months then independence, personal cell number, video form feedback, programme changes on communication, and the chasing message: 'hey, Omar, what are you doing?' His response was 'No, that's, yeah, definitely. Definitely what I'm looking for.' Confirmed rather than enthused. Notably he then immediately reduced it to something he could plausibly do alone — 'it's pretty simple at that point, right? Like, working on it isn't hard' — which the rep countered well ('it's simple, but it's not easy'), but the seed of the DIY objection is visible right there.

anchors.raw: if I wanted to take the additional time, you know, I could go online and say, hey, show me some kettlebell workouts, tell me what to eat, right? And then I have to sift through all that and then kind of figure that out.
anchors.competitor: free online kettlebell content and self-directed research
anchors.note: The decisive anchor and it was never touched. He states the alternative and concedes its weakness in the same sentence — the sifting, the time cost — which is exactly the opening to sell the value of curation and accountability. The rep answered a different question instead.

anchors.raw: I have a buddy who is in that space... He's trained professional athletes... he has been big on kettlebell workouts, and he's always talking about eating clean. Now, this is somebody that I know and I trust.
anchors.competitor: a personal friend who is a professional strength coach
anchors.note: Double-edged and the most interesting anchor on the call. This friend is why the prospect took the meeting at all — he pre-validated kettlebells and clean eating, which is why the method met zero resistance. But he is also a free, trusted expert, and the prospect explicitly contrasted him with the rep: 'this is somebody that I know and I trust. You guys right now, unfortunately, you're a stranger to me.' The one thing the friend cannot give is availability — 'he's just so busy with his clients and he's in Mexico now' — which is the exact gap the offer fills. The rep did not use it.

anchors.raw: I'm going to go back and look at, you know, my current gym membership and kind of everything that I'm already doing and see kind of, am I removing that stuff to incorporate this, am I doing it in addition to
anchors.competitor: his existing private gym membership, boxing training and group classes
anchors.note: He is already paying for coaching-adjacent services he values and enjoys, including sparring and mitt work, so the offer is competing for a budget line that is currently occupied rather than empty. He framed the decision explicitly as replace-or-add. Nobody asked what the gym costs, which would have been the obvious way to size the comparison.

anchors.raw: it will be anywhere between thousands and nine thousands depending on duration... 1,000 to 9
anchors.note: An anchor the rep created, before discovery was finished, in response to the prospect asking for pricing structure. The prospect immediately went hunting for the bottom — 'where does the 1,000 fit? Where does the 9,000 fit and everything in between?' — and had to be told the cheap end buys generic programmes rather than personalisation. Disclosing a $1,000 option and then quoting $6,000 makes the headline price a choice rather than the price.

anchors.raw: there's other things. There's projects going on, yards and all that, right? So it's just making sure that that additional $6,000 on top of everything else, every other project that's being done is going to make the most sense for me.
anchors.note: Not an affordability constraint but an allocation one — he is choosing between this and other things he wants. This is the anchor that OC cannot touch, because there is no financial picture to build; the money exists and is spoken for by preference.

anchors.raw: $6,000 is not a small amount of money. It's not a large amount of money. It's kind of, you know, it's a decent amount
anchors.note: He explicitly places the price inside his range twice, and separately confirms 'I'm doing well'. Combined with a successful career, international business travel and a private gym membership, capacity is not in doubt — which is precisely why treating this as a money objection would have been the wrong read.

unmet_demand.want: A way to train the programme where he actually lives — hotels and Latin American gyms where kettlebells are often unavailable
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He raised it unprompted as one of his two main concerns and got no real answer: try to find a gym, most probably have them, and solve it yourself. The programme does appear to have the answer — the rep mentioned calisthenics and maces thirty minutes later in a different context, and claimed many clients travel heavily — but it was never connected to the blocker, so from the prospect's side this demand is still open. The substance almost certainly exists; nothing was said when it mattered.

unmet_demand.want: Something concrete to evaluate before committing $6,000 to a company he first encountered the previous day
unmet_demand.why_unmet: There is no proof asset to send and no written breakdown of deliverables. He had to ask twice to get a verbal description of what the money buys, and the rep's own framing was 'it's not like there is a thousand details to it.' He is a salesperson evaluating a salesperson and said so; the absence of anything tangible reads to him as an absence of substance. The same gap appeared on the Edward Garcia call in this batch.

unmet_demand.want: Programming that works around an elbow at 8-9 out of 10 on pushing and pulling movements
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He described modifying or abandoning exercises mid-session because of this elbow, and it was never addressed. Kettlebell work is pressing and pulling heavy. Video form review plausibly catches it in practice, but nobody confirmed the programme can be built around a joint that currently limits him, and the mobility pillar was pitched as making everything better without qualification.

unmet_demand.want: A comparison that shows why this method beats the alternatives he intends to research
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He said plainly he would 'weigh it versus other methods' and possibly go with 'another person or company'. The offer has no positioning against substitutes — not against free content, not against in-person training, not against his existing gym. When asked what else he was considering he could only say 'another way to accomplish the same types of things', and the rep's answer was to clarify that it is not only kettlebells. There is nothing in the sale that tells a buyer why this rather than that.
